Write short notes (what you changed, any surprise) to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/astra-p4-2-notes/notes.md (create the directory).

OWNED FILES: storygame/runtime/item_facts.py, storygame/runtime/capture.py, storygame/runtime/engine.py (edit); tests/test_refused_move_clause.py (new). Edit nothing else.

PROBLEM: The narrator's prose can claim a physical move (e.g. 'Kristin carries the laptop to the truck'). After the turn is committed, capture (WorldCapture.after_commit in capture.py, calling ItemFactsProvider.apply_item_facts in item_facts.py) may REFUSE that move; today the refusal is only an issue string and the player-visible reply still asserts the move. DESIGN (decided by the owner): an ENGINE-COMPOSED CLAUSE. When capture refuses a move, the engine appends one short deterministic segment to the reply saying the thing did not move. No LLM call, no re-narration, no regex over prose.

REQUIRED CHANGE:
1. item_facts.py: add a per-turn list `self._last_item_facts_refused` (reset at the start of apply_item_facts exactly where `_last_item_facts_unplaced` is reset; also initialise wherever that one is initialised) holding dicts {"name": <entity label>, "id": <entity id>} for each REFUSED move. The refusal sites are the two places that append "...refused place ...": in `_apply_move` (when `not result.ok` after the unplaced fallback does not apply, i.e. the generic 'refused place' issue) and the 'fixed things cannot move' branch. Do NOT record 'left unplaced' cases, 'refused because it is hidden' cases, or any non-move refusal. De-duplicate by entity id. Add `last_item_facts_refused(self)` returning a copy, next to `last_item_facts_unplaced`.
2. capture.py: include `"refused": _json_value(self.provider.last_item_facts_refused())` in the dict `after_commit` returns, and add the new attribute name to every per-turn attribute list in capture.py that already lists `_last_item_facts_unplaced` (the save/resume lists around lines 139-171), so save/load between commit and follow-up keeps working.
3. engine.py: add a small private method, e.g. `_refusal_segment(self, capture_record)`, that returns a `NarrationSegment(kind="narration", text=...)` or None. Text: for the refused entities, 'Name has not moved.' for one, 'A and B have not moved.' for several (join with ' and ', use 'has'/'have'), where Name is the entity's player-facing label (use the label helper the item_facts provider already uses, `provider._entity_label(world, id)`, so an unnamed person shows as 'the man watching Kristin'; capitalise the first letter). Skip entities that are hidden. Append that segment to the result's `segments` on the normal committed path in `turn()` (next to where `entry_segments`/`resolution_segments` are appended) and on the resume path that also calls `self.capture.after_commit` (around line 557-580), so both paths show it. Do not add it on game_break returns or rejected turns. Record that a clause was added in the `capture_issues` as 'refusal clause added for <name>' (via the existing delivery.capture_issues update; one extra string is fine).

TESTS (new file, hermetic, no network, no live worker): use a real RuntimeEngine with the real package data/stories/continuity-initiative and a stub narrator whose reply claims a move, plus a stub capture/match reply so that capture REFUSES the move. Study tests/test_item_facts_null_place.py, tests/test_unknown_identity_not_creation.py, tests/test_pipeline_eval.py and bench/pipeline_eval/runner.py (PipelineArm drives a stub-narrator RuntimeEngine with a WorldCapture) for how to build the engine and force a refusal; the pipeline_eval refusal cases in bench/pipeline_eval/cases.json show a command that is refused (a fixed thing cannot move). Cases: (a) a refused move adds the final segment 'X has not moved.' and the joined narration ends with it; (b) an accepted move adds no clause; (c) a 'left unplaced' result adds no clause; (d) two refused entities give the 'have not moved' form; (e) the clause is added on a save/load round-trip between commit and follow-up if the existing tests show how to do that cheaply, otherwise state in notes why not. If a case cannot be built as described, adapt to the nearest real behaviour and say so in notes; never weaken (a).

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside the cwd. Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_refused_move_clause.py tests/test_unknown_identity_not_creation.py tests/test_item_facts_null_place.py tests/test_bench_item_facts.py tests/test_pipeline_eval.py tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py. Also run `-k "item_facts or capture or engine or world_model or narrated"` over tests/ and report failures; if an existing test asserts the old exact narration of a refused move, update that test to expect the clause and list it in notes (add it to nothing else). Ruff: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix and -m ruff format on every file you changed. Reply with the files changed.
